mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 7.5% over a 3-month period, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 7.5% over 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when both HOUST and RSAFS decline simultaneously in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply contraction regime (industrial production below 100), manufacturing output declines, leading to reduced corporate profits and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO is below 100, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% over a 3-month period signals the start of monetary tightening, which increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5% over 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate improving consumer confidence and residential investment, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST increases, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer spending and corporate hiring, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as earnings growth expectations rise.
failure_condition: The positive return signal fails when both PAYEMS and RSAFS increase simultaneously in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS above 0.5%), the Federal Reserve's policy shift increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is negative.
